hardware.tested_state: flash-encryption blocker added to runtime signing-readiness policy

procedure: Added flash_encryption_enabled to the host-core SigningReadiness gate.
Updated the host-core signing-policy test so signing remains blocked unless flash_encryption is present with the other M8 gates.
Ran nSealr/esp32 make ci with 37 Python tests, host-core tests, and firmware validation.
Built the T-Display S3 firmware with ESP-IDF v5.5.4 from /Users/vincenzo/esp/esp-idf-v5.5.4/export.sh.
Confirmed the ESP-IDF build reported app version 46eb8dd.
Ran the default USB serial smoke suite with 33 verified exchanges.
expected_result: The firmware with the stricter flash-encryption signing-readiness gate still builds, flashes, and preserves the disabled signing protocol contract.
observed_result: The 46eb8dd firmware built successfully, flashed on /dev/cu.usbmodem1101, and passed 33 USB serial smoke exchanges: 6 response frames and 27 expected rejection frames. sign_event remained signing_disabled.
limitations: This is a readiness-policy hardening smoke, not production signing acceptance.
Flash encryption is required by policy but is not enabled on this development scaffold.
The protocol response for sign_event remains signing_disabled.
No persistent key custody, secure boot, flash encryption, debug-lock, enclosure, or production approval policy was validated.
